title: CV
text:
Alex Marshall Durham, NH | 815.980.2594 | alexmarshall216@gmail.com EDUCATION University of New Hampshire, Durham, NH Anticipated Graduation: May 2028 Bachelor of Science in Marine, Estuarine, and Freshwater Biology
GPA: 3.9 • Trustee’s Scholarship • Dean’s List, Highest Honors, Fall 2024, Spring and Fall 2025 Coursework: Honors Introductory Biology: Evolution, Biodiversity and Ecology with Lab, Honors Contemporary Conservation Issues, Ecology, Honors Introductory Biology: Molecular and Cellular, Introduction to Marine Biology, Organic Chemistry SKILLS AND CERTIFICATIONS Field Skills: Species identification; quadrat and transect sampling; data recording; use of field guides; use of pH/temperature probe; use of PAR sensor; mist net handling; bird extraction Lab Skills: Report writing; maintain detailed lab notebook; gel electrophoresis; density separation; PCR; DNA extraction, microscopy, thin layer chromatography RESEARCH EXPERIENCE UNH Coastal Restoration and Resiliency Lab, Durham, NH
2025-Present Undergraduate Researcher • Filtered and sorted coastal sediment samples as part of microplastics research • Processed bog sediment cores through homogenization, organic digestion, and density separation to examine microplastic content through a microscope • Collaborated on poster Are Microplastics Ubiquitous in Freshwater Wetlands for the April 26th, 2025 UNH Undergraduate Research Conference Rockford University Bird Banding Project, Rockford, IL
Volunteer August-November 2021-2023 • Set up mist nets once a week in the forest, maintaining them during workdays by removing debris, disentangling roughly 20 birds an hour, and deterring predators
• Recorded data, including weight, tarsus, wing length, sex, and approximate age, on roughly 20 birds a week, from a variety of songbird species • Worked with other members of the project to efficiently remove birds in the least amount of time possible, while avoiding deterring other birds from entering the mist nets WORK EXPERIENCE Community Foundation of Northern Illinois Internship, Rockford, IL
Intern • Coordinated outreach to underserved communities within the service area Summer 2025 • Conducted archival interviews with donors • Supported youth program engaging local teenagers with philanthropy Severson Dells Nature Center, Rockford, IL Summer Camp Staff Summer 2023 – 2024 • Assisted with camp preparation and childcare in a nature-based education setting • Developed knowledge of Illinois forest and prairie ecology
• Maintained garden and natural playground through weeding CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS AND POSTERS Franzoni, C., Marshall, A., Wilkins, L., Ciampitti, R., Jarrett, G., and G. Moore. (2025)
Are Microplastics Ubiquitous in Freshwater Wetlands? Examination of Peat Deposits in a Remote Atlantic White Cedar Bog in Bradford, NH. Undergraduate Research Conference, 26 April 2025, University of New Hampshire, Durham, NH CAMPUS ACTIVITIES New Hampshire Youth Movement, Durham, NH Volunteer • Helped to plan campaigns to improve student life on campus • Attended rallies at the state capital to generate support for university funding • Spread awareness on campus of youth issues University of New Hampshire Campus Democrats, Durham, NH 2025-Present August 2024-Present Volunteer • Participated in activities like canvassing and phone banking to encourage voting and gauge support for Democratic candidates • Attended weekly meetings to discuss the state of politics in New Hampshire
